hero.tagline: From 2016 to 2046, Coding Girls Club builds a bridge between women and programming.
hero.title: Building a bridge across the divide
hero.description: Founded in 2016, 程序媛汇 (Coding Girls Club) is a social enterprise. In the beginning, we taught women to code and helped them enter and stay in tech; today, AI is redefining human society as a whole, and in this transformation, we want more women to master technological and AI capability for their own daily lives, work, and careers. 2046 is the deadline we set for ourselves: thirty years of doing this properly — year after year, starting with a class, an event, a peer to connect with.
hero.quote: “Our mission is digital empowerment for women, and we pursue it with humble persistence.”

entries.text: Coding Girls Club founded; the first coding workshop held.
Selected for the UNDP “Tech for Good” project casebook.
Awarded in the CYLC National Youth Social Organizations Partnership Program.
Paper with Carnegie Mellon University researchers published at ICSE CHASE 2021 (IEEE).
The thirty-year promise fulfilled — we are on our way.

journey.note: We also supported the UNDP & UN Women #科技遇见她# one-hour coding challenge.

agentConnect.notesDesc: If you already have other MCP server entries, merge the cgc-2046 entry into the existing config — don't overwrite it. The token is bound to the user, not the workspace, so joining a new workspace needs no reconfiguration.

agentConnect.installedPanel: Once installed, a “程序媛汇 2046” (CGC-2046) panel appears in the sidebar and a “CGC-2046 assistant” appears in your conversation list.
agentConnect.generateTokenDesc: If automatic connection is unavailable, use the manual path: issue a connection token on the MCP page (bound to user, not workspace), copy it, then tell the “CGC-2046 assistant” in OpenClacky that you've copied it — the assistant reads the clipboard safely and the token never enters the conversation log.
agentConnect.assistantConnectHint: (Manual token fallback) After copying the token, go back to OpenClacky and open the “CGC-2046 assistant” conversation — tell it you've copied. The assistant reads the clipboard safely and completes the connection; the token never enters the conversation log. Until this step runs, your agent can't reach the platform yet.
agentConnect.oneClickConnectDesc: After installing CGC OpenClacky, open the local OpenClacky app and click “Connect website” in the “程序媛汇 2046” (CGC-2046) panel. The assistant will guide you through CGC browser login and configure MCP automatically—no token copy required.
agentConnect.dshInstallDesc: In DSH (minimum version 0.1.2), run the following command to install the CGC-2046 plugin family (dsh-cgc-all):
agentConnect.dshManualFlowDesc: Once installed, return to step ③ below to issue a connection token and copy it — then tell the agent in DSH "connect to CGC-2046" and it completes the connection in one step from your clipboard (the token never enters the conversation); you can also paste it manually into the connection form of the "CGC-2046" panel in the DSH sidebar — both paths are equivalent.
agentConnect.dshIntegrityHint: Package integrity: dsh-cgc-all is published by the official CodingGirlsClub organization (verifiable via npm provenance). Check the source before installing — beware of lookalike packages that steal tokens.
agentConnect.dshClipboardHint: The token is shown in plain text only once; clear your clipboard after connecting so it doesn't linger on other devices via clipboard sync.
